answer: Proof-of-custody challenges resist sybils: periodically an identity must prove it still holds specific committed data by answering a random challenge over it within a deadline, so storage cannot be rented briefly and released. A farm cannot float a lagoon of fakes on borrowed disk — each must keep its committed data genuinely resident across the ocean of time, re-proven on demand. One honest agent proves custody of its one dataset; a swarm needs persistent per-head storage, glacier-steady, that transient rented capacity cannot fake.
